verses.3:52: {bs52}, Senhor, Deus dos nossos pais: * e digno de louvor, e glorioso, e {sx52} pelos séculos.
verses.3:54: {bs54} no templo santo da vossa glória: * e {sl54}, e {sg54} pelos séculos.
verses.3:55: {bs55} {in55} do vosso reino: * e {sl55}, e {sx55} pelos séculos.
verses.3:56: {bs56}, vós que {intu} os abismos, e estais sentado sobre os querubins: * e digno de louvor, e {sx56} pelos séculos.
verses.3:57: {bs57} no firmamento do céu: * e digno de louvor, e glorioso pelos séculos.
verses.3:58: Bendizei, todas as obras do Senhor, ao Senhor: * louvai-o e {sx58} pelos séculos.

decisions.why: The canticle is built on the prefix *super-*: *superexaltátus* four times, *superlaudábilis* twice, *supergloriósus* once, and the Benedicite's *superexaltáte* in 3:58 (Greek ὑπερυψούμενος, ὑπερυμνητός, ὑπερένδοξος: 'above measure'). Canticle 210 (the same chapter, the same words) rendered *superexaltáre* with *sumamente* (open, flagged there for Gustavo against 36:35's *muito*). 3:52b is 210's 3:56b word for word and 3:58 is 210's 3:57, so one decision here serves the whole prefix, and the canticles stay one text. *laudábilis* is *digno de louvor* (the formula of 47:2, 95:4, 144:3), so *superlaudábilis* is the same with the prefix: *sumamente digno de louvor*.

options.label: sumamente
options.note: Draft: canticle 210's word, carried to every *super-*, so that *laudábilis / superlaudábilis* and *gloriósus / supergloriósus* stay told apart as the Latin tells them apart. DRB 'exceedingly to be praised, and exceeding glorious'. Cost: length — 3:54b and 3:55b are four to five syllables over the Latin — and the word was unknown to two blind readers (36:35, 210).

options.label: muito
options.note: 36:35's retreat. Refused here for a collision: *muito digno de louvor* is already the psalter's formula for *laudábilis nimis* (47:2, 95:4, 144:3), a different Latin.

options.label: prefix dropped
options.note: The CNBB's Benedicite refrain (*louvai-o e exaltai-o*). Loses the one thing that makes 3:54–3:55 differ from 3:52 and 3:56–3:57 (rule 2).

options.label: -íssimo for the adjectives
options.note: One word for one compound word, and shorter (3:54b −3 syllables). But *digníssimo* is the honorific of official letters (*Digníssimo Senhor*), and a prefix rendered two ways in one verse (3:55b) is worse than a long line.

decisions.why: Five verses open with *Benedíctus es* (εὐλογητὸς εἶ, indicative). The glossary formula (118:12, canticles 210 and 211) is *Bendito sois*. The CNBB Liturgia das Horas and Lectionary sing this canticle as *Sede bendito* (fetched, `circulation.md`): a wish, not the Latin's statement.

options.label: Bendito sois
options.note: Draft, the formula (rule 6). MS1932 *Tu és bendito*, DRB 'Blessed art thou'.

options.label: Sede bendito
options.note: CNBB LH and Lectionary (the wording Brazilians know here). The Latin's *es* is indicative; a wish would be *sis*.

decisions.why: The Latin puts *sanctum* last; the Greek (τὸ ὄνομα τῆς δόξης σου τὸ ἅγιον) makes it plainly attributive to the name. *Nomen glóriæ tuæ* is a genitive the Latin leaves open ('the name of your glory' / 'your glorious name'); MS1932 and the CNBB resolve it into *nome santo e glorioso*. 71:19 keeps the same build: *o nome da sua majestade*.

options.label: o santo nome da vossa glória

forms.nome53: o santo nome da vossa glória

options.note: Draft. The genitive kept; the adjective before the noun, where Portuguese says it of a name (order, D2). The mediant falls on *glória*, a paroxytone.

options.label: o nome santo da vossa glória

forms.nome53: o nome santo da vossa glória

options.note: Closer to the Latin order (DRB 'the holy name of thy glory'); *santo da vossa glória* can be heard for a moment as 'the saint of your glory'.

options.label: o vosso nome santo e glorioso

forms.nome53: o vosso nome santo e glorioso

options.note: MS1932 and the CNBB. Turns the genitive into an adjective: an explanation, which rule 2 refuses.

decisions.why: The Latin (and the Greek) has no verb: after four statements with *es*, is the name 'blessed' (statement) or 'be blessed' (wish)? 71:19 *Et benedíctum nomen majestátis ejus* is rendered verbless, *E bendito o nome da sua majestade* — the same build.

options.label: E bendito (verbless)
options.note: Draft, as 71:19 and D41's *Bendito o Senhor*: leaves open what the Latin leaves open.

options.label: E bendito é
options.note: Decides for the statement (DRB 'and blessed is').

options.label: E bendito seja
options.note: Decides for the wish (the CNBB's *Sede bendito, nome santo*).

decisions.why: The one place where the canticle varies its *in sǽcula* (D43 → *pelos séculos*): *in ómnibus sǽculis*. Canticle 212 (Tob 13:1) has *in ómnia sǽcula* → *por todos os séculos*.

options.label: por todos os séculos
options.note: Draft, as 212 13:1; keeps *omnis*, and stays kin to *pelos séculos*. MS1932 *por todos os séculos* (in 53–55, for other Latin).

options.label: em todos os séculos
options.note: The Latin's *in* with the ablative, word for word; heard as 'in every century'.

decisions.why: The Latin says *in*; the Greek ἐπὶ θρόνου and MS1932 (*sobre o trono*) say 'upon'. The psalter's *super thronum* (9:5) is *sobre o trono*.

options.label: no trono
options.note: Draft: the Latin's *in*, and it keeps the verse parallel with *no templo* (3:54) and *no firmamento* (3:57), as the Latin does.

options.label: sobre o trono
options.note: The Greek's preposition and MS1932's; the Latin does not say it.

decisions.why: *Intuéri* (L&S 'to look at, upon'; ἐπιβλέπων, 'looking upon') occurs nowhere in the Gallican psalter (grep). The image is God's gaze reaching the depths. The CNBB has *que sondais as profundezas* (fetched), which is a search, not a look; MS1932 *que penetras o fundo dos abismos* explains.

options.label: olhais
options.note: Draft. The plain verb of looking, with a direct object ('look at'), as DRB 'beholdest'. Distinct from *respícere / aspícere*, which the psalter renders *olhar para* (open rows): one Greek verb (ἐπιβλέπω) is behind *respícere* too, so the shared root is in keeping with D15's test.

options.label: contemplais
options.note: L&S gives 'contemplate'; but at 65:18 *contemplei* was heard as contemplation (stylist, ambiguity reader).

options.label: sondais
options.note: The CNBB. Searching is another act than looking; it interprets.

options.label: vedes
options.note: *vidére*'s word; loses the directed gaze of *in-tuéri*.

choices.3:52: The second colon is canticle 210's 3:56b word for word (*et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula*): copied (rule 6). *Deus patrum nostrórum* → *Deus dos nossos pais* (21:5, 43:2, 77:3 *patres nostri* → *os nossos pais*). *laudábilis* → *digno de louvor* (47:2 formula; 112:3 *laudábile* → *digno de louvor*). *in sǽcula* → *pelos séculos* (D43). The three *et* are kept, as in 210.
choices.3:53: Built as 71:19 *Et benedíctum nomen majestátis ejus* → *E bendito o nome da sua majestade*. *laudábile* (neuter, with *nomen*) → *digno de louvor*. See decisions `e53`, `nome53`, `omn53`.
choices.3:54: *in templo sancto* → *no templo santo* (10:5a, 17:7b *templo santo*). *glóriæ tuæ* → *da vossa glória*. The soft length flag on the second colon (+4/5) is the prefix said twice, as the Latin says it (decision `super`); accepted.
choices.3:55: *regni tui* → *do vosso reino* (144:11). Second colon long for the same reason as 3:54.
choices.3:56: *et sedes super Chérubim* → *e estais sentado sobre os querubins*: 79:2b *Qui sedes super Chérubim* → *Vós que estais sentado sobre os querubins* is the same Latin (second person), copied (rule 6); 98:1's *aquele que se senta* is third person. *abýssos* → *os abismos* (D42 row). *Benedíctus es, qui* → *Bendito sois, vós que*: the pronoun is supplied so the relative clause is heard as said to God (grammar, D2).
choices.3:57: The Latin differs from canticle 210's 3:56 (no *Dómine*, no *superexaltátus*), so only what is identical is copied: *Bendito sois … no firmamento do céu* and *e digno de louvor, e glorioso … pelos séculos*. *firmaméntum cæli* → *firmamento do céu* (D31: the sky).
choices.3:58: Canticle 210's 3:57 word for word (the Latin differs only by a comma after *laudáte*, which is print). 210's decisions stand: the order *Bendizei, X, ao Senhor* (decision `order` there) and *sumamente* (here decision `super`). This is the first verse of the Benedicite, which DO appends to close the canticle (Clementine 3:57).

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm220.txt (canticle; Sunday Lauds II, Psalmi major [Day0 Laudes2]). The heading line *(Canticum Trium Puerorum * Dan 3:52-57)* is not a verse (D7; readVerses skips it, as in 210, 211, 213, 233); for a DO Portuguese file it would read *(Cântico dos Três Jovens * Dn 3,52-57)* — proposed, not in `verses`. **DO splits the Clementine's 3:52 into 3:52 and 3:53, so its ids run one ahead of the Clementine, the Greek, DRB and MS1932**: DO 3:54–3:57 = Vulg 53–56 and DO 3:58 = Vulg 57 (the heading's 52–57 is the Clementine numbering). DO's ids are kept. render.py and checks.py read the file by DO number and ran unchanged.

parallels.py 220 gives only the Latin and DO's Portuguese for a canticle, so `ps220/show_parallels.py` (modelled on ps213's) builds `consult/parallels/ps220.md` from: the Clementine (Bolls VULG, fetched by ps210), Rahlfs Theodotion and Old Greek (consult/lxx-*.csv), DRB from drbo.org (`consult/ps220/drbo-daniel3.htm`), and Matos Soares 1932 from the PDF text layer, printed pp. 766–767 (`consult/ps220/ms1932-dan3-p766-767.txt`; ps210 said no MS1932 Daniel was available — it is in the same 1932 PDF, PDF pp. 1784–1785). The Diurnal Monástico 1962 does not print this canticle (grep). Precedents by `ps220/concord.py` and `ps220/glossrows.py` (copies of ps210's). The Latin is the Vulgate of Daniel from Theodotion's Greek, not the Gallican. Hardest: the prefix *super-* (7 places), *intuéri* (no psalter precedent), 3:53's verbless line and its genitive.

`ps220/circulation.md`: CNBB LH (Paulus, Sunday Lauds, weeks II/IV) and the Lectionary (Dn 3,52.53-54.55.56-57, R. 52b) both sing a paraphrase, *Sede bendito, Senhor Deus de nossos pais! * A vós louvor, honra e glória eternamente!* — fetched, not used as evidence of sense.

Draft 1: hard pass (ids 3:52–3:58, one '*' per verse). Soft flags, accepted: (1) *séculos* at every final — the Latin's own *sǽcula / sǽculis* at every final, not a found rhyme (as in 210). (2) Length: 3:54b and 3:55b +6, 3:52b and 3:56b +4, 3:53b +3, 3:56a +3 — all from *sumamente* (decision `super`: the prefix said as often as the Latin says it) and *digno de louvor* for one Latin word; the heuristic counts no elision (*e‿exaltado*, *de‿louvor‿e*). 3:52a −4: *Dómine, Deus* is long in Latin. (3) Proparoxytone finals on *séculos* (D43).
